summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. AI stocks wobbled worldwide and the NZX 50 slipped 0.6% on Friday, but still finished its third straight week of gains.

New Zealand is still in limbo after the 7 November election. On preliminary results the National–ACT–NZ First coalition holds 67 of 131 seats, but final results with about 400,000 special votes aren't due until 27 November.
Fuel costs keep squeezing Kiwi wallets. Petrol is around $3.64 a litre and core retail spending fell another 1.2%.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down
stories.summary: Huang resigned with immediate effect after reports about his personal conduct, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% before closing 4.3% lower, and all three major US indexes ended about 0.4% down.
stories.why: Nvidia is around 6% of the S&P 500 and the face of the AI boom, so its leadership shake-up affects most global share funds, including KiwiSaver.

stories.headline: NZX 50 dips Friday but logs a third weekly gain
stories.summary: The index hit a record 14,259 on Thursday, helped by Mainfreight's strong result, then gave back 0.6% on Friday. Gentrack was the biggest faller and Vista the biggest riser.
stories.why: The NZ market is up 4.6% for the year to date, despite election uncertainty and high fuel costs.

nz_politics.headline: Election still too close to call until the 27 November count
nz_politics.summary: Preliminary results give National 42 seats, Labour 36, Greens 16, ACT 13, NZ First 12, Opportunity 7 and Te Pāti Māori 5, in a parliament enlarged to 131 seats by overhang. The incumbent coalition is two seats over the majority line.
nz_politics.why: Nearly 400,000 special votes could still shift seats, and serious coalition talks are unlikely to start before the final result.

nz_politics.headline: Opportunity Party enters Parliament for the first time
nz_politics.summary: Led by Qiulae Wong, the party cleared the 5% threshold with about 6% of the vote and seven seats. It says it is open to working with either bloc.
nz_politics.why: If the special votes narrow the gap, Opportunity could decide which side governs.

world.headline: US-brokered Russia–Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi
world.summary: Russian and Ukrainian officials met on 10–11 November for the first US-brokered talks since February, focusing on postwar security and de-escalation. European leaders want a ceasefire before any broader security talks.
world.why: Any progress would ease energy and food price pressure in Europe and beyond.

world.headline: COP31 climate summit underway in Antalya, Türkiye
world.summary: The summit runs 9–20 November, with energy security and electrification at the centre after the Iran war disrupted Gulf oil supply. Major new deals are seen as unlikely.
world.why: The Iran conflict is the main reason petrol prices in New Zealand are near record highs.

stories.headline: Fuel costs are crowding out other spending
stories.summary: Stats NZ data shows core retail spending dropped another 1.2% as Kiwis spent more on fuel. ANZ's Truckometer also showed heavy traffic down 0.4% last month.
stories.why: When household budgets tighten, discretionary services like window and gutter cleaning are often among the first to be put off.

stories.headline: Markets lean towards an OCR hike on 9 December
stories.summary: After two rate hikes, the Reserve Bank surprised by holding the OCR at 2.75% in October. Traders still see a December hike as likely, and the Financial Stability Report is out on 17 November.
stories.why: A hike would push up mortgage and business loan rates, but also lift savings rates.

marketing.headline: Maybelline changes its 35-year-old tagline
marketing.summary: 'Maybe she's born with it' now reads 'Maybe we're born with it', aiming for inclusivity while keeping one of beauty's best-known lines.
marketing.why: This is a textbook case of refreshing a brand asset without throwing away the recognition built up over decades.

marketing.headline: Meta and Google ad changes land before Black Friday
marketing.summary: Meta Pixel began measuring conversions on customer devices on 12 November, and Google Ads changes how customer lists are uploaded from 16 November. Meta's new ad terms apply from 20 November.
marketing.why: If you run Facebook or Google ads for Coastal Clear Windows, check that your tracking still reports correctly.

weather.note: Settled and warm through Tuesday. Wednesday looks wet, so book outdoor jobs earlier in the week.

term.definition: Under MMP, if a party wins more electorate seats than its share of the party vote entitles it to, it keeps the extra seats and Parliament grows beyond 120. That's why this Parliament could have 131 MPs.
term.example: Te Pāti Māori won 5 electorates on 0.6% of the party vote, so most of those seats are overhang.
